entry.title: Three new claims: whether more shark-bite victims survive than in past decades ( C44 ),…
entry.content: Three new claims: whether more shark-bite victims survive than in past decades (C44), whether Hawaii's tiger shark season is tightening as the water warms (C45), and what Queensland's shark-control gear catches besides tiger, bull and white sharks (C46). Two pairs that asked the same question were merged: C2 into C16, now "The bull shark season off NSW is getting longer", and C37's drone check into C6. C32 has a first look: El Niño and La Niña don't explain the extra warm months off Sydney.

entry.content: Every grade change now says why it changed, in the claim card's own words, instead of "New data changed the result". The five changes of 12 November have their reasons filled in: C1, C4, C21, C25 and C29. The claim groups on Research now use the same three questions as Home.

entry.title: A fourth group of claims, "How people change the sea", with six claims on energy, land,…
entry.content: A fourth group of claims, "How people change the sea", with six claims on energy, land, fishing and habitat (C32–C36, C41). Five more ask sharper questions: drone sightings per flight hour (C37 (now part of C6)), young bull sharks in southern nurseries (C38), detections before bites (C39), whether people follow closures (C40) and other warm-water species moving south (C42). Every claim now names what it is measured per. C25 adds temperatures measured by tags on five bull sharks in South Africa, and was retested with daily sea temperature: tagged bull sharks in Florida's Manatee River overwinter in water well below 19°C, and so do some small bull sharks in the Clarence River in NSW, while large sharks in Sydney Harbour leave before winter. Its grade moves from "supports it" to "leans toward it". A new claim, C43, tests the explanation: of NSW bull sharks tagged under 150 cm, most were detected in winter; of those tagged at 200 cm or more, few were. C1 moves to "no clear link": a study that allowed for fishing effort (Banaghan et al. 2025) found no clear rise in southern catch rates. C3 is now graded straight from the data; C2 (now part of C16), C6, C16 and C24 cite the new Queensland studies. Every tested claim now carries an "Evidence" line with its tier, from measured at the shark down to bite records with no count of people, and the tier caps the grade (see "How claims are graded"). A review of the claims that rest on bite records alone moved two to "First look": C4, whose test did not measure when baitfish run, and C21, which rested on six bites. C29 moved from "points the other way" to "leans the other way", because strong upwelling also keeps people out of the water. C24 stays ruled out, with a note on bull shark bites at Réunion and New Caledonia.

entry.title: Every claim now uses one grading scale (see "How claims are graded"), set from the data.…
entry.content: Every claim now uses one grading scale (see "How claims are graded"), set from the data. C5 and C24 are now Ruled out; C29 points the other way; C2 (now part of C16), C9 and C20 are First looks; C4 and C21 lean toward their claims, and C1 moves to "leans toward it" because share of catch stands in for catch per drumline. Every graded card now opens with "Where this stands": what was tested, what came out, why it has its grade, what would change it, and how the grade has moved. C16: held to listening stations, the later departures from Sydney weaken; now "leaning later, not settled". C30: first look at public tagging data for young white sharks. Result wording now updates with the data.

entry.title: C5 : white sharks keep the whales' calendar but not their numbers. New white shark…
entry.content: C5: white sharks keep the whales' calendar but not their numbers. New white shark claims: C29, upwelling, not supported so far; C30 (nurseries) and C31 (seals), open for testing. C6: Queensland's drumlines catch twice as many bull sharks when rivers run high. New claim C28, rain and tiger sharks: not supported so far. C18 people or sharks: bites lean to weekends in California and New Caledonia, and faintly to hot, calm days. C5 whales leans that way; tides (C24) and greener water (C4) show nothing yet.

entry.content: C7 warm current: rerun with the Bureau of Meteorology's Fremantle record, which runs to March 2026. 4 of 5 checkable bull shark bites since 2020 came in stronger-than-usual months, still too few to rule out chance.
